hook: In a chat window you prompt into the void; in Huabu, an agent starts from the context you have already laid out on the canvas.
lede: Working with AI usually means working in chat, and chat runs in one direction: ideas, documents and agent outputs pile up in separate sessions, each out of sight of the others. Huabu, an open-source desktop workspace from Microsoft Research Asia, replaces the thread with an infinite surface. Thoughts, files, open questions and agents share one Space as visible, connected nodes that persist across sessions, so a person and their agents work from the same context. Long Ling helped build it from 0 to 1 during her internship, exploring new ways to organize knowledge, maintain shared context and let agents take collaborative actions.

chapters.title: Prompting into the void
paragraphs: The project site starts from a plain observation about working with AI in chat: a conversation runs in a single line, and thinking rarely does. The useful pieces, a note here, a document there, an answer from an earlier session, end up scattered across chat histories and sources, each one visible only from inside its own thread.

Huabu’s answer borrows from an older shift. The desktop gave files and programs one surface to meet; Huabu aims to do the same for thoughts, sources, tasks and results in the agent era, bringing them onto one shared thinking surface.

quote.text: Chat is linear, but your thinking is not.

chapters.title: Everything you bring becomes a node
paragraphs: Work in Huabu happens in a Space, an infinite canvas. You can pull a thought out of a conversation, or drop in a PDF, a website, an image, a video or a file, and each arrives as a visible node that can be placed, revisited and connected to the others. Ideas, notes, documents and outputs from different chat sessions end up side by side instead of in separate windows.

The Space also outlasts the session. Materials stay visible and connected from one session to the next, and each Space lives in a local folder that the user chooses as their Home when Huabu first launches.

chapters.title: Where a note sits is part of the thought
paragraphs: On a canvas, layout carries meaning. Research can be arranged by time or by direction, then connected into readable context for both the person and their agents, so the structure itself becomes part of what gets communicated.
AI can take part in that work, arranging information, uncovering relationships and clarifying ideas. The person stays in charge of the canvas, reviewing and controlling every change the AI proposes.

quote.text: Position is part of the thinking, not decoration.

chapters.title: Agents that begin with your context
paragraphs: Users bring their own agents into a Space. There, an agent can understand not only the materials it has been given but also how those materials relate to one another, which helps it grasp what the person intends and do more relevant work.

That changes what a request looks like. Agents begin with the context already in the Space, so you give them a brief rather than a blank-page prompt. Several tasks can run in parallel, and every result comes back to the Space, where it can be arranged and built on like everything else.

chapters.title: Your folder, your models, your review
paragraphs: Huabu does not bundle an LLM service: people connect a model provider of their choice, which may require a separate account or usage charges, and can connect external coding agents. When an AI feature runs, that provider may receive the prompt and the relevant Space content, and external agents may read or modify files in the working directory configured for them.
points: Spaces and their materials are stored in the Home folder the user selects.
Huabu sends no telemetry, crash reports, diagnostic logs or usage data to Microsoft.
Packaged desktop builds encrypt saved credentials using storage protected by the operating system.
It is released for research and experimental use: AI output may be inaccurate, incomplete, biased or unsafe, and should not drive high-risk or time-critical decisions without qualified human review.

takeaways: Moving from a chat thread to a canvas makes context something you can see and keep: ideas stay where you put them, across sessions.
Arrangement doubles as communication: how materials relate to one another helps agents grasp intent, not just content.
Human judgment stays in the loop, from reviewing every AI-proposed change to keeping work in a local folder with the models the user chooses.
